title: Object as Hotspots: An Anchor-Free 3D Object Detection Approach via Firing of Hotspots

problem.summary: Another unique property and challenge of LiDAR point clouds is the sparseness. LiDAR points lie on the objects’ surfaces and meanwhile due to occlusion, selfocclusion, reflection or bad weather conditions, very limited quantity of points can be captured by LiDAR.

evidence.quote: Inspired by compositional part-based models [4, 5, 6, 7, 8], which have shown robustness when classifying partially occluded 2D objects and for detecting partially occluded object parts [9], we propose to detect objects in LiDAR point clouds by representing them as composition of

Inspired by compositional models, which represent an object as parts and their spatial relations, we propose to represent an object as composition of its interior non-empty voxels, termed hotspots, and the spatial relations of hotspots.

Based on OHS, we design an OHS detection head with a hotspot assignment strategy that deals with interobject point-sparsity imbalance by selecting a limited number of hotspots and balancing positive examples in different objects.

experiments.summary: Experimental results show that our proposed method works remarkably well on objects with a small number of points. Our approach achieves real-time speed with 25 FPS on KITTI dataset.
